subject: Re: [Incident] Streaming responses stalling / very high per-token latency
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@firenet.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@firenet.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming responses stalling / very high per-token latency

Hi Monica / Marissa,

We started seeing severe degradation on our chat streaming for the 08:00 PST deploy window — tokens are intermittently stalling (no data for 3-10s) and when responses resume they come in 800ms-2s per token which is unusable for our UX. This started at ~07:45 PST and is affecting ~30% of active sessions.

We tried increasing client-side timeouts but the stream either disconnects or resumes with huge gaps. Non-streaming generate calls are nominal. Can you confirm whether anything changed in the service and advise immediate mitigations? We can repro on EU and US endpoints.

Sample: session id 2a7b-9f8c — first stall at 07:48:13.

--
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform
Firenet AI

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@firenet.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:20:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responses stalling / very high per-token latency

Alex — thanks for the report and the session id. We're investigating as a priority.

Immediate asks while we dig in:
- Could you attach a small client HAR / tcpdump of a failing session if possible?
- Can you confirm whether the sessions are pinned to a model (e.g. redwood/v1-stream) or using auto-routing?

Short-term mitigations you can try immediately (low friction):
- Switch the request to non-streaming generate (stream=false) for critical flows — this avoids the streaming chunk path.
- Reduce chunk_size / max_tokens_per_chunk in your client to 64 tokens.
- Implement a client-side fallback: if stream stalls for >2s, close and retry once with non-streaming.

We'll follow up with an ops status update within 30 minutes. Attached: snapshot-logs-20260715.tar.gz (please reply if upload fails).

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Quick status and what we're doing now — looping in engineering: dev, we're seeing elevated tail latency in streaming worker pods in us-west and are applying a routing policy change + temporary autoscale bump.

Alex — please try the following immediately and report results: 
1) Short-term client change (2-5 min): set stream=false for non-interactive background flows; for interactive flows set max_tokens_per_chunk=64 and stream_chunk_timeout_ms=1800.
2) Use the regional fallback: hit api.us-east.redwood.ai (we've routed some traffic away from the affected us-west workers).
3) If you can, enable client-side incremental polling with a 1s backoff when a stream stall >2s is detected.

We expect to have a rollback or targeted fix within ~45 minutes. We'll keep you updated every 20 minutes.

Monica

From: dev.patel@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:06:37 -07:00
Subject: RE: Streaming responses stalling / very high per-token latency

FW: ops findings and mitigation plan.

Root cause (preliminary): a recent kernel-selection optimization (ktv2) caused regression in KV cache eviction heuristics under certain sequence-length distributions. That produced frequent small cache thrashing on us-west streaming workers which surface as intermittent upstream stalls.

Action in progress:
- Rolling back the ktv2 kernel-selector change on the affected pool (targeted rollback rolling update).
- Bumping streaming worker ASG min capacity by +20% for us-west for the next 90 minutes.
- Enabling conservative routing policy for customers using streaming (forces routing away from canary pools).

ETA: patch & redeploy started; we expect streaming latency to normalize in ~35-50 minutes. Will post when rollback completes and when the canary is validated.

Internal refs: runbook-internal/STREAM-KV-EVICT (internal) | patch: patch-ktv2-rollback-20260715

- Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@firenet.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and long-term mitigation guidance — Firenet streaming disruption (7/15)

Alex — thanks again for your patience while we resolved this. Below is a short summary and recommended actions you can take on your side to harden against similar incidents.

Timeline (short):
- 07/15 07:45 PST — Firenet reports intermittent stream stalls and elevated per-token latency.
- 07/15 08:00 PST — Our telemetry shows increased tail latency on us-west streaming worker pool.
- 07/15 08:25 PST — Engineering identified a regression tied to ktv2 kernel-selector impacting KV-cache eviction.
- 07/15 09:15 PST — Targeted rollback and autoscale bump completed for affected pools. Telemetry returned to baseline by ~09:30 PST.

Root cause: a kernel-selection change that altered eviction behavior for the KV cache under certain workloads, causing frequent small cache evictions and stalls on streaming workers.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations you can adopt (recommended order):
1) Non-streaming fallback: switch critical responses to non-streaming generate while the incident is ongoing. This is the most reliable short-term mitigation.
2) Chunking: configure client to request smaller streaming chunks (max_tokens_per_chunk=48–64) to reduce sensitivity to micro-stalls.
3) Stream timeout+retry: if no chunk arrives within 2s, close the stream and retry once with stream=false.
4) Regional fallback: route to api.us-east.redwood.ai as a secondary endpoint during incidents.
5) Prefix caching: maintain a short client-side prefix cache for repeated system prompts to reduce token volume at startup.

Longer-term recommendations and product changes we're planning:
- Improved kernel-selector canarying and additional performance telemetry for KV eviction rates.
- Streaming client-side guidance and SDK helper to auto-fallback to polling.
- New conservative routing policy toggle for accounts that prefer lower tail-latency risk.

Attachments: postmortem-20260715-firenet-highlatency.pdf (summary + timeline + action items).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review with SREs next week to walk your platform engineers through the incident and the recommended SDK changes.

Thanks again — apologies for the disruption.

Best regards,
